question: What is the primary purpose of a Drug Revolving Fund in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To guarantee a continuous and steady supply of essential medicines
options.B: To generate maximum profit for the hospital management board
options.C: to provide free medications exclusively for indigent citizens
options.D: To fund capital building projects within the hospital premises

explanation: The DRF mechanism exists primarily to prevent stockouts of critical pharmaceuticals by maintaining a self-sustaining pool of funds dedicated exclusively to drug procurement. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is keeping the DRF account separate from the general hospital overhead account important?

options.A: It eliminates the need to ever restock inventory through external suppliers
options.B: It allows the federal government to tax pharmaceutical sales directly at source
options.C: It prevents funds generated from drug sales from being diverted to other operational expenses
options.D: It ensures that doctors receive higher commission bonuses on prescribed drugs

explanation: Ring-fencing DRF revenue ensures that money collected from patients goes straight back into buying more drugs rather than paying utility bills or unrelated administrative costs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h1)

question: What term describes the initial money used to establish a Drug Revolving Fund and purchase the first stock of medicines?
explanation: Seed capital provides the foundational financial backing required to purchase the very first inventory of medications before sales revenue can take over. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h2)

question: How does the initial government grant function within the lifecycle of a DRF?

options.A: It serves as a monthly stipend to cover the salaries of hospital pharmacists
options.B: It is paid back with high interest directly to the central ministry of finance every month
options.C: It remains sitting in a bank vault as collateral for international loans
options.D: It acts as a one-time injection that transitions into a self-sustaining cycle through patient sales

explanation: Government grants or seed money are meant to kickstart the process, after which the fund sustains itself independently through the continuous cycle of sales and restocking. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary source of operational revenue for most hospital-based Drug Revolving Funds?

options.D: Direct grants from the World Health Organization

explanation: Patient purchases at hospital pharmacies supply the constant cash flow required to keep the revolving cycle active on a daily basis. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h3)

question: A public hospital relies entirely on patient user fees to sustain its DRF, but widespread poverty in the community leads to low drug sales. What is the most immediate threat to the DRF?

options.A: Excessive accumulation of cash surpluses in the pharmacy vault
options.B: Automatic reduction of physician prescribing habits across all departments
options.C: Inability to raise enough capital to place the next bulk drug restocking order
options.D: Immediate intervention and takeover by international pharmaceutical companies

explanation: If cash inflows from patient payments drop significantly, the fund loses the liquidity required to purchase new inventory, leading directly to stockouts. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h3)

question: How do health insurance schemes contribute revenue to a hospital's Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: By paying salaries directly to the nursing staff working in the dispensary
options.B: By paying direct claims and reimbursements for medications given to enrolled patients
options.C: By providing free vehicles for transporting drugs across state borders
options.D: By imposing fixed monthly fines on patients who fail to visit the clinic

explanation: Managed care organizations and health insurance agencies reimburse healthcare facilities for the drugs provided to their registered members. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a major operational challenge when a DRF relies heavily on health insurance reimbursements?

options.A: Hospitals are legally prohibited from purchasing drugs from local manufacturers
options.B: Insurance agencies automatically dictate the retail price of all hospital services
options.C: Delays in processing and paying claims can create cash flow shortages for restocking
options.D: Patients refuse to accept brand-name medications from the pharmacy

explanation: Slow reimbursement cycles from insurance administrators can tie up vital capital, making it difficult for the pharmacy to purchase new drug stock on time. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a reliable permanent source of internal DRF capital?
explanation: Donor grants are time-limited and subject to change, making them unreliable as a permanent foundation for a self-sustaining revolving fund. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why must healthcare managers exercise caution when integrating international donor drugs into a standard DRF?

options.A: Government regulations forbid mixing donated items with locally purchased inventory
options.B: Sudden cessation of donor programs can lead to abrupt stockouts if the fund has not built internal reserves
options.C: Donor drugs are universally substandard and harmful to patients
options.D: Patients will refuse to take medications that do not carry local brand names

explanation: Because donor support is temporary, facilities must prepare to transition patients back to self-funded procurement models before grants expire. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h5)

question: What purpose does the modest markup added to drug prices serve in a DRF?

options.A: To cover operational costs and generate a surplus for restocking
options.B: To pay off the personal debts of the chief pharmacist
options.C: To fund luxury travel for hospital board members
options.D: To satisfy federal luxury goods taxation laws

explanation: The controlled markup ensures that losses from wastage and inflation are offset while building a surplus to purchase larger volumes of drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h6)

question: How do retained earnings protect a Drug Revolving Fund against economic inflation?

options.A: They allow the hospital to freeze all employee salaries indefinitely
options.B: They eliminate the need to ever buy medications from foreign manufacturers
options.C: They automatically increase the purchasing power of the national currency
options.D: They build up extra financial reserves that offset the rising wholesale cost of imported drugs

explanation: As prices rise, having accumulated surpluses ensures the fund still holds enough aggregate capital to purchase necessary inventory volumes. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is a direct consequence of poor inventory management and high medication expiration rates within a DRF?

options.A: Increased willingness of patients to pay higher prices for medications
options.B: Gradual depletion of capital and eventual collapse of the drug supply chain
options.C: Automatic subsidization of the pharmacy by international health banks
options.D: Rapid capitalization and expansion of the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Expired or unaccounted-for stock represents lost money that cannot be recovered, directly shrinking the pool of capital available for future purchases. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h7)

question: A ward nurse notices that several boxes of intravenous fluids in the treatment room are nearing their expiration date while fresh stock sits at the front. What action best supports the DRF principles?

options.A: Transferring the older stock to a private pharmacy for cash sale
options.B: Ensuring the older stock is used first following proper stock rotation principles
options.C: Hiding the older stock in a drawer until it officially expires
options.D: Throwing away the older boxes immediately to keep the shelf clean

explanation: Practicing First-In, First-Out (FIFO) inventory management prevents wastage and protects the financial capital tied up in pharmaceutical supplies. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h7)
